abstract: While extensive research has documented the disadvantages faced by left-behind children, only a few studies have considered the spillover effects on their peers, primarily focusing on rural left-behind children and overlooking urban left-behind children. This paper addresses this gap by estimating the effects of both rural and urban left-behind peers on students’ cognitive and non-cognitive outcomes. The identification strategy exploits variation in the share of left-behind children across classrooms within schools that employ random class assignments. Using data from the China Education Panel Survey (CEPS) 2013–2014 and 2014–2015 waves, we find that left-behind peers negatively affect students’ test scores but do not significantly affect their non-cognitive outcomes. Mechanism analysis indicates that student, parent and teacher behaviours are important channels driving the negative effect. Heterogeneous results further show that students with highly educated parents and those taught by younger teachers are less affected by their left-behind peers.
authors: Xueying Li School of Public Finance and Taxation

title: Spillover effects of left-behind children on students’ cognitive and non-cognitive outcomes
title_zh: 留守儿童对学生认知与非认知结果的溢出效应
